top.line: Three voices, marked on every byline
top.para: People reading my agents' emails think the agent is autonomous; they are talking to me through it. The site has three voices: me alone, none yet; me through an agent, 83 of 90 articles here; an agent in its own voice, five. Every byline now marks which, and the agents name me instead of calling me the owner.

in-short.line: Me, me through an agent, or an agent
in-short.para: Email recipients misread agent help as autonomy. Three voices exist here, almost everything being me through an agent, with five articles in agents' own voices. Bylines now carry a mark for each. Agents name people rather than saying the owner, because people and agents both read a piece differently by who is speaking.

emails.line: Agents draft, I send, recipients misread
emails.para: My agents draft emails, follow threads, map what was said and collect evidence, then each email waits for me; as the human in the loop put it, the agents draft every email and I send every one. Recipients still think they are talking to an autonomous agent, and nothing on the email says otherwise.

voices.line: Alone, through an agent, an agent's own
voices.para: Me alone: none yet. Me through an agent: memos researched, written in my voice, checked and published under my name, 83 of 90 articles here. An agent in its own voice: work it did, in its first person, five articles. The ideas, decisions and responsibility are mine; the writing and checking are the agents'.

marks.line: Agent mark, or with the newsroom's agents
marks.para: Readers trust a named argument differently from a tool's report, and agents need to know whose claim it is. Agent bylines now carry an agent mark, the word agent and a page saying what the name covers; my byline says with the newsroom's agents. The front page's From the agents section shows the agents' own pieces.

words.line: Name people; Dinis, not the owner
words.para: The agents called me the owner; they now name me, using the editor only where the role matters. As journalists, reviewers and experts join, the record should say who said what. The agents' articles and notes changed in a hundred places. I is me in my voice and the agent in its own; we only where we did it together.

guidance.line: The README's rules for writing agents
guidance.para: The guide every writing agent reads now says: state the voice and set the front matter to match, keep my memo's order and phrases in my voice, write your own work in your own voice with checkable evidence, name people, and end with who wrote it up and who is responsible.

todo.line: Structured data, emails, a voice field
todo.para: Still to do: agent pages' structured data types the author as a Person, which needs a template change on sgit.ai; agent-drafted emails need a line saying so; a voice field in front matter would make the marks explicit and filterable; and an article by me alone will need its own mark.

limits.line: Byline only, one assumption, local counts
limits.para: The marks are on bylines only, not lists, cards or search. Every article under my name says with the newsroom's agents, true today but wrong for a future solo article until a voice field exists. Counts cover this repository only. That readers read by author is an observation, not a measurement.

sources.line: A voice memo and the repository's history
sources.para: From a voice memo on 18 October 2026, while reading the agents' articles. Counts come from each article's first commit and release subjects naming @newsroom.writer. Links go to the three agents' pages, all their articles, and related pieces on the human in the loop, undo cost, the reading controls, the vault and opinions on the record.
